steps.title: Sweat onion
steps.text: Rinse fresh produce under running water before peeling, cutting or zesting, including the lemons, dill, shallot and horseradish; follow any prewashed or ready-to-eat arugula label. Heat the assigned oil from {{ingredients}} in a skillet. Cook the onion about 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent without browning; transfer all the onion and cooking oil to a mixing bowl.

steps.title: Grind fish
steps.text: Keep {{ingredients}} cold during preparation; check for bones. Pulse in a food processor until coarsely ground, then add to the onion bowl. Do not grind to a smooth paste.

steps.title: Bind
steps.text: Stir {{ingredients}} into the fish and onion until evenly combined. Add one ninth of the measured lemon juice here and reserve the remaining eight ninths for the salad. The original batch uses 1 tsp juice here; scale that share with the listed juice total. All the measured cream, matzo meal, eggs, carrot, dill, lemon zest, water, salt and pepper belong in this mixture.

steps.title: Prepare pan
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, line the bottom and sides of a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving overhang to fold over the surface. Spread all the mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it and cover with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap. Multiples need separate original-size loaves and baths; smaller amounts need appropriate smaller pans and earlier center checks. Keep comparable mixture depth and headroom rather than forcing every scale into this pan.

steps.title: Water bath
steps.text: Place the loaf pan in an original-batch 9-by-13-inch baking dish, or a suitable larger outer vessel, and carefully add {{ingredients}}. Support the hot vessels securely and keep bath water out of the fish mixture.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 325°F, checking near the original 1 hour 15 minute planning time. Continue until a thin-tip thermometer in the center reaches 160°F /71°C and the center is firm. Check the center of every separately baked loaf; a firm surface or clean knife alone does not replace the measured endpoint.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.text: Remove the loaf pan carefully from the hot bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly at 40°F /4°C or below, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Chill at least 4 hours until cold throughout before inverting and peeling away the parchment. Making it the day before allows cooling and chilling without rushing.

steps.title: Finish salad
steps.text: Toss {{ingredients}} together just before serving. Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, {{ingredients}}. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.

before: Keep raw fish refrigerated until preparation. Thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator and follow any vacuum-pack instructions about opening the package before thawing. Keep raw-contact tools separate from cooked fish and garnishes.
Use boneless skinless fillets, checking for remaining bones; keep the fish and mixing tools cold during preparation.

checkpoints.cue: The center reaches 160°F /71°C and is firm; check every loaf.
checkpoints.why: This fish mixture contains raw eggs and must set at the center; ordinary fillet 145°F guidance does not replace the saved 160°F endpoint.

troubleshooting.cause: Terrine was unmolded before fully chilled or fish was ground to a paste
troubleshooting.fix: Chill until cold throughout before unmolding and slice with a clean sharp knife. Chilling may improve slicing, but cannot restore coarse texture once fish has been overprocessed.

after.timing: Allow about 30–45 minutes active, roughly 1 hour 15 minutes baking subject to the center check, brief cooling and at least 4 hours chilling. after.storage: Keep cooked terrine refrigerated at 40°F /4°C or below, cooling promptly within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Use within 3–4 days, with salad separate. Serve cold from refrigeration and promptly return unused portions; if choosing to reheat stored terrine, reach 165°F /74°C throughout.

## Chef's Note

This baked salmon-carp terrine modernizes traditional Passover gefilte fish. Pulse fish in food processor just until coarsely ground, not paste - this ensures meaty texture. Baking in a water bath (bain-marie) helps cream and eggs set into silky, souffle-like structure. Serve chilled with fresh horseradish salad for brightness.

## Directions

1.  **Sweat:** Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a skillet. Sauté the onion for 8-10 minutes until soft and translucent (do not brown).
2.  **The Grind:** Pulse the carp and salmon in a food processor until coarsely ground. Transfer to a large bowl with the onions.
3.  **Bind:** Stir in the cream, matzo meal, dill, the measured salt and pepper, eggs, shredded carrot, lemon zest, and 1 tsp of the lemon juice. Whisk in 3/4 cup cold water until smooth.
4.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 325°F. Line the bottom and sides of a 9x5 loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving enough overhang to fold over the surface. Spread the fish mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it, and cover the pan with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap.
5.  **Bain-Marie:** Place the loaf pan inside a 9x13 baking dish. Fill the larger dish with boiling water until it reaches halfway up the loaf pan.
6.  **Bake:** Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until the center is firm (160°F).
7.  **Set:** Remove from the water bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour if the room is above 90°F / 32°C). **Chill for at least 4 hours**, until cold throughout, before inverting onto a platter and peeling away the parchment. Allow at least 5 hours 45 minutes for preparation, baking and chilling, plus cooling time; making it the day before gives more flexibility.
8.  **Finish:** Toss arugula, radishes, and horseradish with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and remaining lemon juice (2 tbsp plus 2 tsp), seasoning to taste. Serve the chilled slices topped with the fresh salad for the mandatory **Acid Balance**.

## Chef's Note

Eli and Max Sussman’s baked gefilte-fish terrine combines salmon with carp or pike and sets in a water bath. Coarsely ground fish gives a different texture from a smooth paste. Keep the full cream and egg binder, allow the loaf to chill throughout, and toss its fresh horseradish salad shortly before slicing.

## Directions

1. **Sweat onion:** Rinse fresh produce under running water before peeling, cutting or zesting, including the lemons, dill, shallot and horseradish; follow any prewashed or ready-to-eat arugula label. Heat the assigned oil from 1/3 of the Olive oil and Medium onion in a skillet. Cook the onion about 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent without browning; transfer all the onion and cooking oil to a mixing bowl.
2. **Grind fish:** Keep Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet and Boneless skinless salmon fillet cold during preparation; check for bones. Pulse in a food processor until coarsely ground, then add to the onion bowl. Do not grind to a smooth paste.
3. **Bind:** Stir Heavy cream, Matzo meal, Large eggs, Carrot, Fresh dill, Lemons for zest, 1/9 of the Lemon juice, Cold water, Black pepper, and Kosher salt into the fish and onion until evenly combined. Add one ninth of the measured lemon juice here and reserve the remaining eight ninths for the salad. The original batch uses 1 tsp juice here; scale that share with the listed juice total. All the measured cream, matzo meal, eggs, carrot, dill, lemon zest, water, salt and pepper belong in this mixture.
4. **Prepare pan:** Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, line the bottom and sides of a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving overhang to fold over the surface. Spread all the mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it and cover with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap. Multiples need separate original-size loaves and baths; smaller amounts need appropriate smaller pans and earlier center checks. Keep comparable mixture depth and headroom rather than forcing every scale into this pan.
5. **Water bath:** Place the loaf pan in an original-batch 9-by-13-inch baking dish, or a suitable larger outer vessel, and carefully add Boiling water for water bath. Support the hot vessels securely and keep bath water out of the fish mixture.
6. **Bake:** Bake at 325°F, checking near the original 1 hour 15 minute planning time. Continue until a thin-tip thermometer in the center reaches 160°F /71°C and the center is firm. Check the center of every separately baked loaf; a firm surface or clean knife alone does not replace the measured endpoint.
7. **Cool and chill:** Remove the loaf pan carefully from the hot bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly at 40°F /4°C or below, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Chill at least 4 hours until cold throughout before inverting and peeling away the parchment. Making it the day before allows cooling and chilling without rushing.
8. **Finish salad:** Toss 2/3 of the Olive oil, 8/9 of the Lemon juice, Baby arugula, Radishes, Fresh horseradish, Shallot, Dill sprigs, Salt for salad, and Black pepper for salad together just before serving. Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.
9. **Serve:** Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, Lemon wedges and Matzos. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.

processGraph.text: Rinse fresh produce under running water before peeling, cutting or zesting, including the lemons, dill, shallot and horseradish; follow any prewashed or ready-to-eat arugula label. Heat the assigned oil from {{ingredients}} in a skillet. Cook the onion about 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent without browning; transfer all the onion and cooking oil to a mixing bowl.

processGraph.title: Grind fish
processGraph.text: Keep {{ingredients}} cold during preparation; check for bones. Pulse in a food processor until coarsely ground, then add to the onion bowl. Do not grind to a smooth paste.

processGraph.title: Bind
processGraph.text: Stir {{ingredients}} into the fish and onion until evenly combined. Add one ninth of the measured lemon juice here and reserve the remaining eight ninths for the salad. The original batch uses 1 tsp juice here; scale that share with the listed juice total. All the measured cream, matzo meal, eggs, carrot, dill, lemon zest, water, salt and pepper belong in this mixture.

processGraph.title: Prepare pan
processGraph.text: Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, line the bottom and sides of a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving overhang to fold over the surface. Spread all the mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it and cover with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap. Multiples need separate original-size loaves and baths; smaller amounts need appropriate smaller pans and earlier center checks. Keep comparable mixture depth and headroom rather than forcing every scale into this pan.

processGraph.title: Water bath
processGraph.text: Place the loaf pan in an original-batch 9-by-13-inch baking dish, or a suitable larger outer vessel, and carefully add {{ingredients}}. Support the hot vessels securely and keep bath water out of the fish mixture.

processGraph.title: Bake
processGraph.text: Bake at 325°F, checking near the original 1 hour 15 minute planning time. Continue until a thin-tip thermometer in the center reaches 160°F /71°C and the center is firm. Check the center of every separately baked loaf; a firm surface or clean knife alone does not replace the measured endpoint.

processGraph.title: Cool and chill
processGraph.text: Remove the loaf pan carefully from the hot bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly at 40°F /4°C or below, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Chill at least 4 hours until cold throughout before inverting and peeling away the parchment. Making it the day before allows cooling and chilling without rushing.

processGraph.title: Finish salad
processGraph.text: Toss {{ingredients}} together just before serving. Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.

processGraph.title: Serve
processGraph.text: Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, {{ingredients}}. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.

capacity: Keep raw fish refrigerated until preparation. Thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator and follow any vacuum-pack instructions about opening the package before thawing. Keep raw-contact tools separate from cooked fish and garnishes.

ratiosYieldAndCapacity.timing: Allow about 30–45 minutes active, roughly 1 hour 15 minutes baking subject to the center check, brief cooling and at least 4 hours chilling. Plan at least 5 hours 45 minutes plus cooling for the original batch; a day-ahead preparation is more flexible. Each pan load changes the actual clock.

shopping: 3 oz Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet

Heat the assigned oil from 1/3 of the Olive oil and Medium onion in a skillet. Cook the onion about 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent without browning; transfer all the onion and cooking oil to a mixing bowl.
2. **Grind fish:** Keep Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet and Boneless skinless salmon fillet cold during preparation; check for bones. Pulse in a food processor until coarsely ground, then add to the onion bowl. Do not grind to a smooth paste.
3. **Bind:** Stir Heavy cream, Matzo meal, Large eggs, Carrot, Fresh dill, Lemons for zest, 1/9 of the Lemon juice, Cold water, Black pepper, and Kosher salt into the fish and onion until evenly combined. Add one ninth of the measured lemon juice here and reserve the remaining eight ninths for the salad. The original batch uses 1 tsp juice here; scale that share with the listed juice total. All the measured cream, matzo meal, eggs, carrot, dill, lemon zest, water, salt and pepper belong in this mixture.
4. **Prepare pan:** Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, line the bottom and sides of a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving overhang to fold over the surface. Spread all the mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it and cover with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap. Multiples need separate original-size loaves and baths; smaller amounts need appropriate smaller pans and earlier center checks. Keep comparable mixture depth and headroom rather than forcing every scale into this pan.
5. **Water bath:** Place the loaf pan in an original-batch 9-by-13-inch baking dish, or a suitable larger outer vessel, and carefully add Boiling water for water bath. Support the hot vessels securely and keep bath water out of the fish mixture.
6. **Bake:** Bake at 325°F, checking near the original 1 hour 15 minute planning time. Continue until a thin-tip thermometer in the center reaches 160°F /71°C and the center is firm. Check the center of every separately baked loaf; a firm surface or clean knife alone does not replace the measured endpoint.
7. **Cool and chill:** Remove the loaf pan carefully from the hot bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly at 40°F /4°C or below, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Chill at least 4 hours until cold throughout before inverting and peeling away the parchment. Making it the day before allows cooling and chilling without rushing.

Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.
9. **Serve:** Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, Lemon wedges and Matzos. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.

8. **Finish salad:** Toss 2/3 of the Olive oil, 8/9 of the Lemon juice, Baby arugula, Radishes, Fresh horseradish, Shallot, Dill sprigs, Salt for salad, and Black pepper for salad together just before serving. Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.
9. **Serve:** Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, Lemon wedges and Matzos. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.
